The presence of the animals has a specific purpose: with their wool, the nuns weave the pallium that the Pope wears on June 29, the Solemnity of Saints Peter and Paul. In the Holy Year 2025, while the rite was taking place, the Pope suddenly fell ill.
film_appearances.Keywords: nuns; lambs; monastery; pallium; pope; rome
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Biennale College Cinema)

film_appearances.Synopsis: The villagers of Sayit are about to receive title deeds, marking the first time in centuries they will claim legal ownership of their land. While this is great news for many, 38-year-old Star faces the risk of losing her home. The title deeds are based on kinship ties, and since her parentage is unknown and she is unmarried, her situation is precarious. Things take a turn when Star discovers a photograph of her younger self in The World Book of Nomads . In the picture, a mysterious hand with familiar tribal markings catches her attention, as she recognises those marks as belonging to a local food seller. Believing the woman to be her estranged mother, Star confronts her, but the woman denies any connection. Desperate to maintain her claim to the land, Star considers several options: finding the foreign photographer who took the picture, proposing marriage to a friend, and signing a morally questionable deal with an NGO. However, this deal puts her at loggerheads with her community.
film_appearances.Keywords: title deeds; land; kinship; mother; ngo; village
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Biennale College Cinema)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Set in a remote Himalayan town during the Kargil War, Secret of a Mountain Serpent tells the intimate story of Barkha, a schoolteacher whose husband is away at the border. In a place where most men are gone and the days echo with silence, Barkha finds herself drawn to Manik Guho, a mysterious outsider who disrupts the fragile balance of waiting, restraint, and myth. As his presence reawakens long- buried yearnings — in Barkha and the other women of the village — a whispered local folklore comes alive: a serpent that lives in the forbidden river, still waiting after a thousand years for the promise of love unkept. This is a poetic exploration of desire and freedom, where myth and memory blur, inviting both women and men into a deeply sensual, haunting journey through love, longing, and transformation.
film_appearances.Keywords: kargil war; himalaya; schoolteacher; serpent; longing
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Biennale College Cinema)

film_appearances.Synopsis: 1968 is communal VR theatre that explores the transformative power of protest through allusions to 1968 — a year charged with societal, cultural and political unrest. Animated from still photographs of both the iconic and the mundane, the piece investigates international interstices of history, human bonding and power in times of socio-cultural upheaval. Rose Bond’s 360° hand-drawn animation interacts with Massimiliano Borghesi’s spatialisation of inti figgis-vizueta’s original recorded tracks of Seven Sides of Fire to ignite a dynamic, evocative and shared immersive experience. 1968 is a collaboration of international creatives and stands as the first movement of a longer, anticipated work. 1968 is experienced collectively under a geodesic sound dome.
film_appearances.Keywords: 1968; protest; history; photographs; music
film_appearances.Visual Style: Communal 360-degree hand-drawn animation VR in a sound dome
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Cartoonist Haru loses his partner, Mina, in the Itaewon tragedy. Since then, 8 pm — the hour she used to come home — keeps repeating: an ordinary moment in daily life now shadowed by her absence. Within that single hour, different emotional rooms unfold. Images and monologues are generated in real time, shaping singular emotional moments. This generative VR experience invites the audience into Haru’s ongoing process of mourning — through the act of constantly drawing and speaking about her.
film_appearances.Keywords: itaewon; cartoonist; loss; mourning; drawing
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: A Long Goodbye tells the story of Ida, a 72-year-old pianist living with dementia. In this animated, interactive VR experience, we walk in Ida’s shoes. We experience a day in her life, as her reality is fading. The apartment, where she spent a lifetime with her beloved husband Daniel, first feels empty and undefined. When we interact with objects and play the tape recordings of her husband, her playful world gradually comes to life, as if drawn in paint before our eyes. Like pieces of a puzzle, memories and conversations help Ida to rediscover herself. But we also discover Daniel’s struggles, as he hopes to stay connected and realises their remaining time together may be short. A Long Goodbye is a poetic experience about the impact of dementia, but above all it is about love and the long goodbye of two lovers who shared a life together.
film_appearances.Keywords: dementia; pianist; husband; memories; love
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Carlo Rambaldi was a visionary architect of the unimaginable. Through his groundbreaking work on E.T. , Alien, and Dune , he expanded the boundaries of cinematic reality — conjuring lifeforms and worlds that defied perception and reshaped the imagination. As we mark 100 years since the birth of Carlo Rambaldi, Alien Perspective resurrects his legacy in a bold new form: a sensory portal into the unknown. At its heart lies Città Spaziale 2 — a never-before-experienced masterpiece where painting becomes a living arena of exploration. Rambaldi’s vision invites us not only to remember but to take part. In the hands of a new generation, the impossible becomes undeniable.
film_appearances.Main Theme: Legacy of a special effects visionary
film_appearances.Keywords: rambaldi; special effects; et; alien; painting
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Director: Doug Liman; Julina Tatlock; Jed Weintrob
film_appearances.Synopsis: Asteroid is an immersive film and interactive story extension made for the launch of Google’s new Android XR platform. The 180° immersive short film is a high-stakes action thriller about a group of strangers who take an old Russian Soyuz rocket to mine a near-earth, treasure laden asteroid for a chance at unimaginable wealth. After the film, the experience continues and the audience enters the world of Asteroid when they receive an SOS from one of the characters, DK Metcalf, who was left for dead. The viewer becomes a player when they are invited to aid in DK’s rescue. Through speaking with an AI-generated version of DK — played by the NFL player as himself — the user determines the truth about what happened on the asteroid and sends his exact location to NASA for rescue.
film_appearances.Keywords: asteroid; mining; rocket; rescue; ai character
film_appearances.Visual Style: 180-degree immersive film with interactive AI extension
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Black Cats & Chequered Flags begins with a haunting Spatial Memory Fragment that immerses viewers in the emotional world of Alberto Ascari. Echoes of his father, legendary driver Antonio Ascari, blend with childhood flashes and the superstitions that shaped his fate. The experience then shifts into high gear with a multiplayer MR pit stop — a collaborative challenge that brings users into the adrenaline and precision of a 1950s Formula 1 team. The journey continues in a stylised VR narrative that weaves archival footage, interactive storytelling, motion capture actors, and immersive sound to explore Ascari’s victories, rituals and tragic destiny. 360° films shot on location in Turin, the Ferrari Museum in Maranello, and the Monza racetrack add historical depth. Ascari — the only Italian double Formula 1 World Champion with Ferrari — was fearless, superstitious, and chivalrous: a man both heroic and haunted.
film_appearances.Main Theme: Life and fate of a racing champion
film_appearances.Keywords: ascari; formula 1; ferrari; monza; superstition
film_appearances.Visual Style: Mixed VR, MR and 360-degree film with archival footage and motion capture
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Blur presents a new myth for the modern age, where science has changed how we think about life and death. With cloning and advances in resurrection biology, we have obscured the boundaries between the living and the dead — the natural and the artificial. This extended reality theatrical production unfolds as a dreamscape, shifting between real and virtual, taking participants on a journey of reflection on grief and eternality.
film_appearances.Main Theme: Grief and the boundary between life and death
film_appearances.Keywords: cloning; resurrection; grief; death; myth
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Collective Body is an interactive, virtual reality experience that invites us to meet ourselves and each other through movement. Set in the middle of a New Mexican storm, participants are guided to rediscover their first ways of engaging with the world, symbolising formative life events that culminate in a shared exploration of our embodied selves. These key moments — beginning alone, discovering the unfamiliar, first encounters, and joyfully moving together — represent how our personal and collective stories are written through movement.
film_appearances.Keywords: movement; body; storm; encounters; collective
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Creation of the Worlds is a VR experience inspired by the visionary art and music of Lithuania’s most renowned artist, Mikalojus Konstantinas Čiurlionis. This poetic VR odyssey is both a meditation on creation and a metaphor for the human journey toward inner maturity. Created by Kristina Buožytė and Vitalijus Žukas, the experience blends immersive storytelling with interactive elements, inviting viewers into a dreamlike world. With the freedom to navigate and soar through evolving environments, the viewer gradually discovers they are not merely an observer — but the creator and caretaker of timeless worlds. Inspired by over sixty of Čiurlionis’s paintings, the experience blends visual art with a contemporary reimagining of Čiurlionis’s music by Phil Von and Rokas Zubovas.
film_appearances.Keywords: ciurlionis; paintings; music; creation; worlds
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Between 1906 and 1954, Henri Matisse created over twenty paintings exploring the theme of dance. This subject shaped many of his artistic choices, influencing his style and technique. Movement and dance were constant sources of inspiration for the master of colour throughout his life’s work. An immersive, dance-led journey through Matisse’s most iconic works, Danse Danse Danse – Matisse invites viewers to step inside his world. Featuring original choreography by Sarah Silverblatt-Buser, in which the user takes part, it pays tribute to the vibrant movements and colours that define his art. This journey into dance and painting grants an intimate view of the creation of some of his greatest masterpieces, including La Danse (1909, The Museum of Modern Art, New York), La Danse de Merion (Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia), La Danse inachevée and La Danse de Paris (Musée d’Art Moderne de Paris).
film_appearances.Keywords: matisse; dance; painting; choreography; colour
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Director: Mads Damsbo; Laurits Flensted Jensen; Anne Sofie Steen Sverdrup
film_appearances.Synopsis: Dark Rooms is an exploration of human psychology through the prism of sexuality. The viewer and two other participants are invited to explore four inner spaces, each one a private, intimate story told and co-created by real people. A unique, embodied experience, guiding the users step by step into the heart of human desire and the shadows it casts. Dark Rooms is a sensory, site-specific and immersive installation that confronts the audience with their own bias and boundaries, exposing our deepest longings and the forces that may shape our sexual identities.
film_appearances.Keywords: sexuality; desire; intimacy; identity; boundaries
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: How do you overcome the fear of the unknown? Eight-year-old deaf Ron is afraid of his first camping trip. To calm him, his mother tells the story of Eddie the Camper, a friendly monster who grew up in the forest and is the perfect companion for a nature adventure. Despite her efforts, Ron, struggles to believe the story, and his fear persists. That night, Ron falls into a deep sleep and awakens in a surreal forest where he meets the player, embodied as Eddie the Camper. Together, they embark on an adventure full of challenges. But there’s one barrier standing in the way: Ron can’t hear, and the player doesn’t know sign language. Across this interactive VR experience, the player and Ron will need to work together to complete tasks like building a campfire, skipping stones in the river, stargazing, and even confronting a menacing carnivorous flower. Along the way, the player’ll navigate the forest, learn simple sign language keywords, and build trust. Will the player and Ron bridge the gap, overcome communication barriers, and succeed in the adventure?
film_appearances.Keywords: deaf boy; sign language; camping; monster; forest
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Inside a lush garden tucked within a busy corporate building, a small, delicate virtual bird flutters. Flaming red, teetering on the edge of burnout, it paces in circles, picks up cigarette butts, and bangs its head against concrete walls... Poor creature — so sensitive, so exposed. It lives, breathes, and feels without skin, mirroring the emotional exhaustion around it. Empathy Creatures is an emotionally intelligent immersive installation — somewhere between speculative fiction and poetic wildlife simulation. Unfolding in two parts, participants encounter an AI-powered being that senses them, talk to them, and gently invites them to slow down, listen and engage in mindful rituals of care. Like a collective Tamagotchi, the work explores emotional co-regulation, collective healing, and our shared responsibility in a fragile, interconnected world. Could a virtual creature help us reconnect with what makes us human?
film_appearances.Keywords: bird; burnout; ai creature; care; mindfulness
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Two strangers’ eyes meet in an elevator — what transformational powers does that moment hold? Face Jumping is an interactive VR short that uses eye-tracking technologies as both muse and platform to explore the impossible desire of seeing through another’s eyes. Visitors navigate a journey of rebirth and evolution by meeting the gaze of other characters and swapping perspectives — including those of birds, rocks, delivery bots, ghosts, cowboys and clouds.
film_appearances.Keywords: gaze; eye tracking; strangers; elevator; perspectives
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Film Title: HeartBeat - son cœur a trouvé sa cadence dans le silence des rencontres
film_appearances.Original Title: HeartBeat - son cœur a trouvé sa cadence dans le silence des rencontres
film_appearances.Synopsis: HeartBeat is an immersive self-performance that explores emotional relationships through the rhythm of the pulse. This installation offers a non- verbal encounter between two strangers, sharing their pulse. This discussion of pulse carries their emotions into a journey — and perhaps, their heartbeats will be in phase.
film_appearances.Keywords: pulse; heartbeat; strangers; encounter
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: The boy’s only friend was a hallucination of his beloved cat. Concerned for his mental health, his mother admitted him to a psychiatric hospital. After three months of medication-based treatment, the hallucinations fade, and he is discharged — but he has lost his emotional anchor and appears even more lifeless than before. Withdrawing into himself, he shuts his mind to the world and isolates in his room. One day, from his window, he sees a girl playing with a stray cat in the parking lot. This quiet moment becomes the catalyst for his recovering.
film_appearances.Keywords: hallucination; cat; psychiatric hospital; isolation; recovery
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: The viewer is part of a group of extras at the Palais Garnier. At the foot of the grand staircase, he crosses paths with Céleste, a young opera singer about to flee the stage. Nervous and unsure, she confides her doubts and dreams to him — torn between the weight of tradition and the desire to find her own voice. Freshly arrived from the provinces, this rising star is about to make her debut in a leading role, but her confidence is shaken. Drawn into her story, the user follows Céleste through the hidden corridors and majestic halls of the Opéra Garnier. As the building comes alive around her, she is transported into iconic scenes from legendary operas — each one echoing a part of her inner journey.
film_appearances.Keywords: opera; palais garnier; singer; debut; doubt
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Film Title: La triste histoire de la petite souris qui voulait absolument devenir quelqu’un
film_appearances.Original Title: La triste histoire de la petite souris qui voulait absolument devenir quelqu’un
film_appearances.Synopsis: Once upon a time, there was a little mouse who worked relentlessly to achieve a single goal: becoming somebody. Driven solely by her ambition, she slowly grew mean and arrogant, pushing everyone away. One day, she accepted a job offer from the most prolific toymaker in the world: Santa Claus. The little mouse was about to discover that climbing the corporate ladder was not all she had hoped it would be... La triste histoire de la petite souris qui voulait absolument devenir quelqu’un is a biting satire of corporate life in the form of a VR Christmas tale.
film_appearances.Keywords: mouse; ambition; santa claus; toymaker; corporate
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Golnaz is a young Iranian immigrant trying to adjust to her new life in Germany. One evening, returning from her job (as an assistant at a migrant reception centre in the Berlin suburbs), she is starving, and her refrigerator is empty. She decides to go to the nearest supermarket. The supermarket has just received a new product: saffron. Even though it is very expensive for her, she cannot resist: she buys a packet of saffron. Emotions overwhelm her. She feels the need to cook a home-cooked meal to help her overcome her homesickness. She prepares rice and adds saffron, a comfort food from her past. But she never expected that this moment would plunge her back into the most traumatic events of her life. Most notably, three years ago, she survived a tragic drowning that took her family while traveling illegally by boat.
film_appearances.Keywords: saffron; iran; germany; migrant; drowning; homesickness
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Mirage is an interactive Virtual Reality experience of a young girl who is battling depression and anxiety. Set in a desert landscape, it is a metaphorical and stylised adaptation with visuals created by the artist Naima Karim and her lived experience with her daughter’s depression and anxiety. The audience embarks on an immersive journey through the young girl’s mind, using hand-tracking interactivity, spatial sound design, original music, and a haptic vest. With hand-tracking interaction, they will be encouraged to support her through her challenges. However, accepting struggles and accepting help from others is not easy for a person suffering from depression and anxiety. Mirage sheds light on the often-misunderstood realities of depression and anxiety, inspiring empathy and understanding.
film_appearances.Keywords: depression; anxiety; girl; desert; mother
film_appearances.Visual Style: Interactive VR with hand tracking and haptic vest
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: In 2125, a century after the green-comet “Emerald Fall,” the alien substance Muk still taints Earth. Two powers remain: Ant City and PAC, a militarised regime ruling from the sea fortress, the Crown. Ant City’s flagship, the ARK — a retrofitted WWII battleship — carries a giant repair mecha meant to restore the city’s shield. PAC plans to hijack the ship, impersonate its crew, and deliver the mecha embedded with malware to disable the shield from within. 18-year-old Mulan, raised aboard the ARK by her father, Captain Hua Muzhi, is unknowingly the only human fully bonded with Muk. Anticipating sabotage, Hua hides in a panic room and locks the engines. As long as he remains hidden, PAC cannot proceed. When the assault begins, AI drone MUV-I is activated and executes Hua’s secret Shan Hai Guan protocol, guiding Mulan through hidden corridors. But her search for Hua accidentally helps PAC mole Aiden trace his location. Aiden detonates charges, separating them, and PAC regains control. Hua reaches the bridge to destroy the mecha but is killed. Mulan awakens Muk’s power, defeats Khan, and fires the main gun — vaporising the Trojan mecha. Muk glows again as PAC retrieves her body. She lives.
film_appearances.Keywords: mulan; battleship; mecha; alien substance; sabotage; drone
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Language: English; Singlish; Cantonese; Teochew; Hakka; Malay
film_appearances.Synopsis: Reflections of Little Red Dot is a mixed reality open documentary that allows viewers to explore the rapidly developing landscape of Singapore through personal stories from Singaporeans young and old alike. With a custom projector, viewers have agency to shape their own narrative experiences, rooting them in the present while looking to the past and forward to the future.
film_appearances.Keywords: singapore; landscape; stories; past; future
film_appearances.Visual Style: Mixed reality open documentary with custom projector
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Where do we go when we zone out, and how do we find our way back to reality? Sense of Nowhere is a journey from no-where to now-here, inspired by The Way from Taoism, the Illusion from Buddhism, and Jung’s practice of Active Imagination. Blurring the line between inner world and outer reality, it transforms sonic, fragmented thoughts into a tangible experience. It is an invitation for the audience to explore the subconscious, piece together hidden clues, and find their way returning to the present moment.
film_appearances.Keywords: zoning out; taoism; buddhism; jung; subconscious
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: A world is made of cubes. The creatures there always follow instructions and push cubes numbly. Yet, when one of them chooses not to follow the instructions, after discovering another path, something unexpected happens.
film_appearances.Keywords: cubes; creatures; instructions; choice
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Film Title: The Clouds Are Two Thousand Meters Up
film_appearances.Original Title: The Clouds Are Two Thousand Meters Up
film_appearances.Synopsis: After the sudden death of his wife, Guan discovers her unfinished novel — a tale intertwining the endangered clouded leopard and the Rukai tribe’s sacred origin myth, which tells of their descent from the elusive animal. Grief-stricken and seeking connection, he sets out on a surreal journey into dreamlike scenes — a maze of the subconscious, mistshrouded forests, ancient tree hollows and symbolic inner landscapes. Adapted from a short story by acclaimed Taiwanese author Wu Ming-Yi, The Clouds Are Two Thousand Meters Up is a single-user, free-roaming VR experience that blends literature and memory into an intimate exploration of love, loss and self-reflection.
film_appearances.Keywords: clouded leopard; rukai; novel; wife; forest
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: For the past three months, Candice has been exploding every day, sometimes multiple times, with a record of seven. She’s now at 192 explosions. Through a visceral VR spectacle, Caroline Poggi and Jonathan Vinel portray her unstoppable anger as a haunting reflection of a world on edge.
film_appearances.Keywords: explosions; anger; girl; rage
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: In The Great Escape , the viewer arrives as the third of three geranium flowers stuck on the windowsill in the bare living room of Patrick, a lonely 38-year-old man. The geraniums are bored to death and constantly frustrated – with themselves, the windowsill, and Patrick. They long to see the world, but are literally rooted in place. Patrick, meanwhile, walks freely but never leaves the house, trapped in his own lonely routine. Every day starts the same: watering the plants, making coffee, feeding his goldfish, activating his roomba, collecting junk mail, then daydreaming by the window. The monotony gets shaken up when Patrick buys a smartphone to connect with the outside world. The geraniums secretly steal it and post a selfie in a plant swap group, where a woman named Sonja spots it. She convinces Patrick to swap the geraniums for her snake plant. The geraniums are thrilled as they venture outside with Patrick, until a chat with a dying bouquet of roses reveals the outside world isn’t so kind to plants. The ensuing existential crisis leads the plants to their near demise and ultimately to a new home with a rather familiar setting.
film_appearances.Main Theme: Loneliness and longing for the world
film_appearances.Keywords: geraniums; plants; loneliness; smartphone; plant swap
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Once a famous TV preacher, the Great Orator died at the height of her fame. Now, her consciousness lives on as an AI, allowing her influence to grow ceaselessly. Her followers can join her again in a shared consciousness, feeding her presence and creating a spiritual singularity. Always changing, shaped by the shared memories of her followers, and therefore unsure of who she truly is. The Great Orator is a nonlinear story world, where the visitor can freely explore and interact with his environment by pointing his hands at objects in the world, no matter how small or ordinary they may seem. Remember: interaction is a choice. The journey will take the visitor to several story spaces in her world: a Preserved House she left behind; a Mainframe storing her followers in a shared consciousness; and an infinite Parking Lot stretching out below, filled with the cars of her followers. Without the visitor, the Great Orator is everything — an infinite number of possible memories and identities — and therefore nothing at all. He chooses which of her stories are true, shaping his own perception of who or what the Great Orator is or was, or if she existed at all. He is family to her, perhaps even more. Each time he visits, her stories are different; the Great Orator is never the same.
film_appearances.Keywords: ai; preacher; consciousness; followers; memories
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Director: Blanca Li; Edith Canat De Chizy
film_appearances.Synopsis: In Andersen’s tale The Shadow , a scientist brings his shadow to life. It becomes autonomous and manages to pass itself off as a human being in society. The shadow overtakes its master, returns to try to enslave him, and ultimately kills him when the latter tries to resist. The evident resonance with our contemporary world and its innovations — both troubling and fascinating — led choreographer Blanca Li to imagine this hybrid creation. Confronted by the dancers of the Compagnie Blanca Li and a percussionist, the audience is immersed in a fantastical universe that blurs perceptions, notions of good and evil and identity.
film_appearances.Keywords: shadow; andersen; scientist; dance; identity
film_appearances.Visual Style: Hybrid immersive dance performance with live dancers and percussionist
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Trapped between waking life and dreams, Olly delves into his childhood memories, navigating the fantastical dreamscapes his sister created to shield them from a fractured home. A journey into the buried past that shapes who we are. His story unfolds across two realms: raw, hand-drawn memories captured in childhood sketches, and surreal underwater live-action dreamscapes. As memory and imagination blur, The Time Before explores the emotional weight of a volatile father, a mother lost in the fog of memory, and a sister who offered escape through imagination and dreams. A meditation on the stories we tell ourselves to survive, and what is lost in the telling.
film_appearances.Main Theme: Childhood memories of a fractured home
film_appearances.Keywords: childhood; sister; father; mother; dreams; memory
film_appearances.Visual Style: Hand-drawn sketches combined with underwater live-action dreamscapes
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: In the frigid waters of the Arctic, diver Ant Williams attempts to shatter the world record for the longest distance swum under ice — on just one breath.

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Ancestors is an interactive and immersive group experience that will make the viewers profoundly connect with the fellow players and with future generations: taking a selfie they become the great great grandparent of a human 200 years in the future. What kind of world will we leave for future generations? Ancestors is a thrilling, collective journey six generations into the future. Guided by viewer’s own smartphone, this interactive experience uses AI to create connections between the players in the room. Together, they will explore the challenges of tomorrow, discovering how collaboration is key to shaping a better world. In Ancestors , participants tell the stories of those who will come after us, stepping into a future shaped by the actions of today. The smartphone becomes the guide, leading the player through a world where the impact of climate change, technological advancements, and social challenges have taken hold. Players’ decisions and interactions shape the narrative and influence the collective outcome of the experience.
film_appearances.Keywords: future; generations; climate change; ai; collaboration
film_appearances.Visual Style: Interactive group experience using smartphones and AI
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Experiences – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Constantinopoliad is a collective reading and audio work. A response to the archive of the poet Constantine Cavafy, the story is inspired by the blank and torn-out pages in Constantinopoliad, an Epic , the journal the teenage Cavafy began when he and his family fled Alexandria; by lost and missing queer archives through time; and by the ghosts, both erotic and historical, that visit the older Cavafy in his poems.

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Eighty years after the end of World War II, this immersive documentary uncovers the untold story of Sgt. Richard Taylor — one of the first to land on Omaha Beach, not with a rifle but with a camera. His mission: to capture the Allied invasion so the world could witness the liberation of Europe. Decades later, his daughter Jennifer receives an unexpected message that launches her on a journey across time and continents to reconnect with the father she never truly knew. Through his restored photos and films, history is brought to life in stunning immersive 3D — transforming memory into an experience you can step into.
film_appearances.Keywords: d-day; omaha beach; camera; father; daughter; wwii
film_appearances.Visual Style: Immersive 3D documentary with restored photos and films
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Experiences – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Life has been going well for Edith. The paranormal detective agency she runs with her flatmate has never been busier, she’s almost up-to-date with her rent and the ghosts in her bathroom mirror have been less demanding than usual. Edith’s world is turned upside down when her brother goes missing and a mysterious new lead promises to reveal clues of his whereabouts. Edith’s journey begins with a visit to a remote Scottish island in the hope a gifted clairvoyant can provide some much-needed answers.
film_appearances.Keywords: paranormal; detective; ghosts; brother; scotland
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Experiences – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: In an Iranian city, Lili, the lonely wife of a militia commander, plots a murder to secure her husband’s rise within a corrupt regime. But when the killing unhinges the order of things, she is drawn into a network of deep web hackers — modern-day witches — who weaponise hidden truth. This stylised neo-noir game adaptation of Macbeth unfolds through smartphones, computer screens, and deep-state surveillance, immersing players as hackers in the oppressive surveillance state.
film_appearances.Keywords: macbeth; iran; militia; hackers; surveillance
film_appearances.Visual Style: Stylised game told through smartphone and computer screens
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Experiences – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: The viewer can travel through three fantastical worlds from author Jack Stevenson’s oldschool Fiendish Fates gamebook series, each featuring different themes and gameplay. With a magical sword in hand, the viewer can make their way through the necromantic Army of Evil , led by the demonic Grey Knight. In Butchers of Orion , they can use mind-powers and body-hopping abilities to escape the slaughterhouse spaceship of the lifesucking Lady Oriana. Moreover, it is possible to blast the corrupt guards of Sheriff Cassidy’s wasteland penitentiary with shock-hand and trusty cyber-shooter in Prisoner of the Cyberhounds . Exploiting interdimensional portals to cross between place, time, and gameplay styles, the viewer discovers clues, secrets, and personal notes to decipher the story behind the books and the true meaning of their journey through Jack’s fictional worlds.
film_appearances.Keywords: gamebooks; sword; spaceship; prison; portals

film_appearances.Synopsis: A WWII submarine crew combats a harrowing torpedo attack in this adrenaline-pumping thrill ride.

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: The Midnight Walk is a reverent dark fantasy adventure built in clay. The player becomes The Burnt One , befriends a lost lantern creature named Potboy, and uses his flame to light your way through a conflicting world of wonder and horror. The aim is to survive and outsmart the many monsters eager to devour Potboy’s flame as the player experiences five tales of fire and darkness, featuring an incredible cast of odd characters. The player can marvel at every disturbing detail in a landscape painstakingly handcrafted with real life clay and animated in a stop motion style — fully playable both on PS5 and in VR (with PS VR2). Everything that can be seen in The Midnight Walk, from the drooling snarl of monsters to the bristling treetops that line the journey was first sculpted in clay and then 3D scanned to a meticulous level of detail. The result is a uniquely layered fantasy world with an artistic imprint; all realized in breathtaking stop motion
film_appearances.Keywords: clay; lantern; monsters; flame; dark fantasy
film_appearances.Visual Style: Stop-motion clay animation game playable in VR
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Experiences – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Wall Town Wonders is a magical mixed reality experience where players discover a miniature town growing inside their living room walls. Through Meta’s latest mixed reality headset, the game blends real and virtual worlds using advanced room scanning and spatial awareness. Players interact with hand-tracked characters, construct buildings, and manage resources, all while discovering secrets hidden behind their walls. The story-driven gameplay unfolds in real-time, reacting to the layout of the player’s home. Detailed animations, expressive motion capture, and immersive sound design make the town feel alive. As players progress, they unlock new zones, residents, and stories, including quests from heroic mice, eccentric inventors, and mischievous goblins. Wall Town Wonders brings childhood imagination into reality, transforming ordinary spaces into enchanted environments filled with wonder, strategy, and storytelling. It redefines home-based gaming, inviting players to play, care, and connect with their tiny walldwelling neighbours.
film_appearances.Keywords: mixed reality; miniature town; walls; mice; goblins
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Experiences – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Film Title: Wayne McGregor: On the Other Earth
film_appearances.Original Title: Wayne McGregor: On the Other Earth
film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Wayne McGregor: On the Other Earth , the world’s first post-cinematic choreographic installation, refracts, evolves and reimagines dance performance in a startlingly original new form of experience. Set within Jeffrey Shaw and Sarah Kenderdine’s radically immersive, panoramic, 360-degree stereoscopic, 12k LED, 26-million-pixel nVis screen, 3D imagery is experienced within an enveloping, largescale cylindrical architecture of eight metres wide and four metres tall. Combining dance, choreography, digital imaging, spatialised sound, and AI, it redefines how we think about movement, the body, and performance. Visitors are invited into the heart of the dance, connecting in close contact with hyperreal dancers in a physicalised sound environment. Never encountered in the same way twice, participants will experience Wayne McGregor: On the Other Earth ’s visual and sonic landscapes unfolding before them in a series of thought-provoking otherworldly encounters and intimate interplay, upending our perceptions of performance and the future of entertainment.
film_appearances.Keywords: dance; choreography; ai; 3d imagery; body
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Experiences – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Synopsis: Arcanum is tough to describe with words. It is a collaboration between rekluma and PK, one creating a beautifully dramatic mix of sound and the other interpreting it with visual shaders inside a cave system. The project was initially presented in Break 15 along with two other shows, Focus and Come Float With Me .

film_appearances.Synopsis: CyberLove | A7 takes place in a dystopian setting where a corporation has taken over much of the planet. The overall series describes a world where unchecked power leads to a warped and uncertain future. In this instalment the player visits an old hotel that has been fitted to be used as a residential housing building. The project itself is a high-detailed environmental piece aiming to mix an immersive, realism-adjacent experience with the social functionality and form that VRChat is so well-known for. The environment showcases the detail, style and originality of content that makes the platform so great! Additionally, the connected storytelling elements give the player the experience of discovering clues about the setting through environmental storytelling.

film_appearances.Synopsis: This project is a faithful fan-recreation of Dracula’s Castle from Netflix’s Castlevania . It’s almost entirely built from scratch and optimized for VRChat. It’s the culmination of more than three years of 3D modeling study and practice, handcrafted to express deep emotions, facilitate exploration, and to inspire other artists to do the same.

film_appearances.Synopsis: The player is in a small exhibition room filled with many works. As he observes them one by one, he gradually begins to notice how the world is structured. By looking behind the works, the player starts to see what lies behind the world itself. exhibition ’s purpose is to discover a new way of seeing the world.

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Do you recall times when everything was simpler? When does life appear vast, full of novelty and unknown? It was a colorful world where happiness required little. The player goes into this world with the creator. Wherever he is and whoever he is, the player and the creator have one place from their common childhood in which they could meet once again. They’ve delayed this journey for too long. The time has come to rediscover this sunlit clearing for himself. What is the player waiting for? Who will be the first to reach the top of the hill? This map is a tribute to a lighthearted period of NOOTAU’s life.
film_appearances.Keywords: childhood; clearing; hill; memories
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: This project is a virtual world where the player floats inside anabandoned elevator shaft surrounded by CRT monitors. The entrance draws from old Hong Kong computer centers, once a bustling hub now fading due to the decline in economy and rise of online shopping. The storefronts are shuttered, plastered with estate ads and posters. As the player walks down the hallway, it warps and dissolves into a surreal space that blends the real and the virtual. It leads to the abandoned elevator chamber, an impossible space that can only exist digitally. xlxxl’s work often reflects a sense of mourning for familiar places and a desire to preserve fragments of them in virtual form. Yet, these memories are inevitably transformed, twisted through the lens of imagination.
film_appearances.Keywords: hong kong; computer centres; crt monitors; elevator shaft; decline
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Flat Earth is a playful and provocative journey through the world of conspiracy thinking. In this satirical VR experience, the player begins as an avatar on the Flat Earth, a disc beneath a shimmering dome. Each region invites the player to shrink down and hear a unique song about the Flat Earth in the local language — from America to Japan. But the journey doesn’t end there. The player leaves the edge of the world and discovers it floating inside a pulsating energy sphere, suspended in space by the Flying Spaghetti Monster. He can go further and escape the boundaries of this strange construct entirely — into the unknown realm beyond the simulation. Flat Earth blends humor, absurdity, and surreal imagery into an immersive, multi-layered exploration of belief, perception, and the stories we choose to follow — or question.
film_appearances.Keywords: flat earth; conspiracy; songs; satire; simulation
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: FZMZ is a masked avatar band born from VR and gaming culture, with members inspired by deep-sea creatures. Active in VR, AR, XR, and real life, they leave a strong impact with music and performances that disrupt both their surroundings and their audience. Their debut song BROKEN GAMES , used as an anime theme, has a double meaning — referring both to buggy, unbalanced games and to the absurdity of modern society. FZMZ’s idea of “destruction” isn’t about negativity, but about breaking norms to inspire courage. To express this, ReeeznD created the immersive space FZMZ Point Zero and produced their first live show, FZMZ 1st Live: DEEP:DAWN . Until now, they existed only in music videos. This live debut not only presents their music but also lets people step into their disruptive world. This project is a raw, unforgettable experience and a striking introduction to their vision.
film_appearances.Keywords: avatar band; deep sea; live show; music; destruction
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

Waving or throwing the orbs makes the particles swirl in beautiful patterns. The player can also use a stick to spawn cubes that interact with the simulation and lighting. He can build a room he likes and relax by watching the ever-changing particles.

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: The player falls asleep in a cosy tree trunk and awakens as Natura, daughter of Mother Nature. They embarks on an enchanting journey through her Queendom, guided by her dreams, wandering through luminous lush gardens, a whimsical mushroom forest, and the vibrant waters of her glacier lake. As the sun rises, it illuminates the Queendom, revealing its splendour. The player traverses magnificent biomes, pausing at breathtaking vistas to admire the surreal, wonder-filled world hand-painted by Anders Fray’s intricate brush strokes and brought to life by the whimsical music of Natura’s celestial friend, Starheart. Her melodies, like guiding stars, lead the player through the luminous Queendom. Transformed into Natura’s avatar, the player can style her dress, hair, and makeup. With the eyes filled with wonder and the mind brimming with imagination, Natura is ready to shine and explore her living Queendom!
film_appearances.Keywords: natura; mother nature; gardens; mushrooms; glacier lake

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: NeoWorlds harkens back to a magical time when virtual world massively multiplayer online games dominated the Internet, asking: what if VRChat was created way back when? The game transforms the VR experience into a 2.5D third person view, interpreting your VRChat avatar as a pixelated sprite. The world features six subworlds hand-crafted in nostalgic pixel-art style, two recreating popular VRChat worlds ( Super VR Ball and The Black Cat , with permission) and four original creations. This experience bridges the player’s earliest memories of online gaming with their most recent virtual world experiences. The latest update introduces player homes, allowing players to acquire furniture and decorate unique spaces.
film_appearances.Keywords: mmo; pixel art; vrchat; avatar; sprite
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: An upside-down tree sparked an idea for a world built around reactive visuals. At its core, Neuron is about turning sound and video into an immersive experience. It is not just a place to watch or listen, it is a world that blends content into its structure, reacting in real time and creating something new with every track. Whether the player is performing, exploring, or just hanging out with friends, Neuron offers a distinct and memorable take on media visualisation. The architecture is inspired by branching neural networks. Structures shift and glow in response to sound, with shaders translating bass, mids, and highs into changes in brightness, color, distortion, and motion. Video textures are layered throughout the world, from walls and floors to particles and fog, creating the feeling that the entire space is alive and moving with the media. Neuron works best with vibrant, high-energy content — transforming them into an environmental experience.
film_appearances.Keywords: neural network; tree; audio-reactive; video; shaders
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: PowderGame is a particle simulation which models interactions between various elements, such as sand, water, salt and fire. To interact with the simulation, you can simply touch the display with any part of your body. Many elements are available, which can be combined in chemical reactions to make new elements. This will sometimes result in explosions, which are modelled using an auxiliary fluid simulation. The particle simulation runs in parallel on the GPU to achieve acceptable performance. The world is a tribute to Dan-Ball’s classic 2007 web game of the same name.
film_appearances.Keywords: particles; simulation; sand; water; fire
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Ritual is an immersion in a five-act psychedelic cycle. The player wakes up again and again in the same abandoned house — an anchor of reality in an ocean of delirium. But with each awakening, the world around mutates: familiar outlines dissolve into chaos of absurd symbols, surreal imagery, and dissonant spaces. Each act is a link in a strange Ritual performed by the player. Is this a dream, a fantasy, or fragments of a troubled mind? Connections remain elusive, leaving a sense of intentional disorientation. The house stands as the sole constant in this visual and narrative vortex, inviting not logical comprehension, but pure, unsettling experience of reality’s disintegration. A world-labyrinth where each act is a new turn in the spiral of madness.
film_appearances.Keywords: ritual; abandoned house; psychedelic; dream; madness
film_appearances.Visual Style: Psychedelic VR world in five acts
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: In this world It is possible to travel across scales, from the tiniest elementary particles to the vastness of the universe. As the player explores, they can dive into a single cell or venture beyond the edge of the galaxy. The scenes transition seamlessly, allowing them to experience the journey as a dwarf or a giant. The behavior of electrons orbiting atoms is simulated based on quantum mechanics, while stars and galaxies are recreated using actual observational data. In other words, this world replicates the fundamental components of the universe as faithfully as possible.
film_appearances.Main Theme: Journey across scales of the universe
film_appearances.Keywords: scale; particles; cells; galaxy; quantum

film_appearances.Synopsis: Filmed inside Virtual Reality and physically in Sweden, this short documentary portrays VR creator Hiyu facing kidney failure, capturing his online friend Photographotter travelling from New York City to Stockholm to be a live donor to him. Formed of poetic montages shot in real-time VR and intimate interviews, rooted in the expressive subculture of the VR community, the film reveals the sincerity of kindness between friends paralleled across realities.

film_appearances.Synopsis: Two familiar worlds collide in this collaboration between VRChat world creators Screaming Color and MetaRick. Somewhere in Uncanny Alley, in what looks like an abandoned factory, lies the entrance to Uncanny Lounge. Uncanny Lounge is a surreal, musical experience where dark cyberpunk decay bursts into vibrant spectacular color. The player interacts with the world to influence the music, reshape the environment, and discover that in these darkest and grungiest of depths, we might find not only a place to hide, but a doorway to a better world...

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: The project was undertaken during a rough time for the creator in late 2024; it was an attempt to put the difficult words into shapes, sounds, and textures in a way that the creator has never done before. The world of vent . is crafted with emotion, not logic, forming a dream-like liminal journey through impossible architecture where the player is an afterthought. It was completed in the tight self- imposed deadline of 50 hours in a style the creator likes to call “emo brutalism”. The player can take some time to sit and listen to the world around you, taking in both the expansive halls and the mundane dead ends to feel out one’s own meaning. There are moments of peace even when things seem to be repeating themselves.
film_appearances.Keywords: emotion; liminal; brutalism; architecture; venting
film_appearances.Visual Style: Liminal VR world in 'emo brutalism' style
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: What Is Virtual Art – Volume 1 is an online virtual exhibition presented by Virtual Museum of Virtual Art (VMoVA). This exhibition is created and curated by Jessien. The captivating art exhibition and narrative explore the vibrant realm of virtual art through the groundbreaking work of four visionary artists: Zeng Chen (reimagining Shadow Play), Polaris (transforming Theatrical Scenery), Li Tianzhi (reinventing Pop-Up Book), and ReVerse Butcher (deconstructing Collage). Drawing inspiration from diverse traditional art forms, they unveil their exquisite virtual creations, offering a glimpse into their creative processes and inspiring broader interdisciplinary exploration.
film_appearances.Keywords: virtual art; shadow play; pop-up book; collage; exhibition
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: This work was inspired by the music of Kikuo, a vocaloid music producer (also known as Vocalo P). This music/art genre originated in Japan and, following the trend of K-pop, is attracting attention from the entertainment industry worldwide. He has a large fanbase all over the world, especially among teenagers, and he completed his first world tour as a vocaloid producer, performing 41 shows in 18 countries. He is also the first vocaloid producer to surpass 100million plays of a single song, Aishite Aishite Aishite . Kikuo is an artist who is constantly pushing boundaries, and his latest passion is VR. His music has the power to help you overcome the hard times that everyone experiences. This work was created in the hope that it will provide a “maniacal perch” for people to visit when they are feeling hazy or heavy.
film_appearances.Keywords: kikuo; vocaloid; music; japan; teenagers
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: When one is surrounded by vast nature, one realizes just how small one really is. SHINONOME BALLOON is a world where it is possible to ride a hot air balloon at dawn, floating above the clouds and taking in the endless sky. “Shinonome” is an old Japanese word that describes the eastern sky turning red at sunrise. Whether one is facing a big life change, starting something new, or just wants to escape the busy everyday life and refresh one’s mind — this balloon ride is ready. It’s a place where quietly reflect on oneself or enjoy a slow, heartfelt chat with someone close. As the player moves through the sky at daybreak, they will enjoy breathtaking views and a mysterious, dreamlike atmosphere. It’s the perfect way to start a journey. This world doesn’t tell a specific story. Instead, it’s a place where each visitor can begin their own new chapter and take home unforgettable memories.
film_appearances.Keywords: hot air balloon; dawn; sky; clouds; reflection
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Best of Worlds – Out of Competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Biennale College Cinema Immersive (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: In the near future, as virtual reality becomes a part of everyday life, creating and using avatars becomes the norm. But what do we choose to project onto these digital selves? Are they idealised versions of who we wish to be — or reflections of our true selves, long hidden within? First Virtual Suit follows a young person who creates their first avatar, only to find themselves on an unexpected journey of self-discovery. As they explore the possibilities of digital embodiment, they are confronted with memories, insecurities, and a version of themselves they had forgotten. In this immersive narrative experience, the virtual becomes a mirror, and the avatar becomes a doorway to the self.
film_appearances.Keywords: avatar; virtual reality; identity; self-discovery; memories
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Biennale College Cinema Immersive – Out of competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Biennale College Cinema Immersive (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Joey believed that happiness was lost to her forever as she grew up. Her shadow, a constant companion, yearned to bring joy back into her life but felt helpless. Nothing changed until the player stumbled into Joey’s inner world through her diary while chasing butterflies. With Dusty, a whimsical dust elf, the player collaborates with Joey’s shadow, using their own shadow to solve puzzles. Together, the player helps Joey confront her deepest fears and defeat the monster lurking within. In Happy Shadow , the player joins Joey’s shadow on an interactive journey, experiencing her confusion and struggles firsthand, and ultimately rediscovering the pure happiness she once knew.
film_appearances.Keywords: shadow; diary; happiness; puzzles; monster
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Immersive - Biennale College Cinema Immersive – Out of competition)

film_appearances.Program / Section: Venice Immersive - Biennale College Cinema Immersive (Out of Competition)
film_appearances.Synopsis: Mnemosyne is an innovative immersive work that blends VR film and live theatre, offering a multi- sensory experience and a poetic exploration of love, illusion, and awakening. Inspired by Tang Xianzu’s Ming Dynasty classic The Peony Pavilion , the piece draws on Eastern philosophy to evoke the notion of “ultimate 情 (Qing/emotion)”. It combines 360° animation, 180° live-action footage, and live performance, with the surrounding environment, shaping each audience member’s evolving sense of presence. The layered narrative unfolds like ink in water: fluid, evocative, and open to interpretation, inviting the audience to drift between constructed memories and imagined futures. Mnemosyne seeks to create a meditative landscape of shifting emotions, centring on the intimate experience of transcending illusion to uncover genuine feeling. It views this hybrid medium of merging physical and virtual presence as a potential stage for exploring the social dimensions and future possibilities of VR/XR.
film_appearances.Keywords: peony pavilion; love; illusion; memory; theatre
film_appearances.Visual Style: Hybrid of 360-degree animation, 180-degree live action and live theatre

film_appearances.Synopsis: This project gives the chance to dive into the legend of Luigi Broglio — who audaciously catapulted Italy into the cosmos from the first space base built on an equatorial sea platform in the 1960s. Within a 360° theatre, audiences become voyeurs to a duel between Broglio and journalist Tristano Malaugurio, two prisoners of fading memory trapped in the ghostly command centre of Kenya’s San Marco space station. Through interviews and flashbacks, we plunge into the African expedition, the explosive encounter with oil giant Enrico Mattei, a near-diplomatic crisis with President Nasser, and a jaw-dropping climax to rewrite history. A group of Italian mavericks daring to compete with the space superpowers. This saga proves that the most impossible dreams ignite into reality when courage meets creativity and determination. Luigi Broglio inspires minds and warms hearts, which is why he deserves to be re-launched!

film_appearances.Synopsis: Allen Nelson was born into a poor family in New York and joined the Marine Corps at the age of eighteen to escape discrimination and poverty. After serving at Camp Hansen in Okinawa, he was sent to the front lines of the Vietnam War in 1966, believing he could become a proud soldier like the war heroes seen in films. But what awaited him there was not glory. On the grounds that the Viet Cong had infiltrated villages, people of all ages were treated as suspects and killed one after another. It was a terrifying and gruesome reality in which he was forced to kill. As Allen took more and more lives, his mind gradually became desensitised. When he returned home at the age of twenty-three, what awaited him were agonising days and sleepless nights, spent haunted by memories of the battlefield. Terrified by loud noises and the dark, his relationships with his family fell apart, and he eventually became homeless. The only thread keeping him connected to the world was Dr. Daniels, a psychiatrist working at a veterans’ hospital, who provided him with counselling and support.

As Leopoldo’s fate appears sealed, unexpected paths begin to open for Maculani and for those seized by doubt. Because a voice may be silenced, but not what it has left in others.

film_appearances.Synopsis: Davide, a thirty-something bookseller, spends his days selling second-hand books in a Roman square. His most devoted customer, Elsa, is also his closest ally: she keeps him supplied with used books and surrounds him with warmth and affection. Then, on what begins as an ordinary day, everything changes. A young boy from North Africa is suddenly thrust into Davide’s care, as though he were a parcel delivered on the street. Silent and unwavering, the child follows him everywhere, like a loyal puppy. When an accident leaves the boy fighting for his life, Davide is forced into a personal descent into hell, haunted by diffidence, guilt and disorientation. One night, in the unlikely sanctuary of a hospital emergency ward, Davide meets Aminah, a teenage girl who has just arrived from Algeria on a migrant boat. Soaked by the rain, frightened and heavily pregnant, she has nowhere to go. Davide can do nothing but take her into his home. It is only the beginning. Night after night, he returns from work to find more strangers living in his apartment. He resists at first, but eventually gives in — out of compassion, or perhaps simply because he cannot say no. His home gradually becomes a shelter for people with nowhere else to turn, those forced to sleep beneath bridges or on the streets. When his neighbours report him to the authorities, Davide is imprisoned for assisting undocumented migrants. What unfolds is an odyssey that extends far beyond his own story, profoundly reshaping the lives of everyone it touches.
film_appearances.Keywords: bookseller; rome; migrants; shelter; prison; child

A balcony, an emptiness, the voices of the street rising up with their obscene vitality – and then the challenge between a grandfather and his young grandson. His grandson is Mario, five years old: a little rascal who speaks like a grownup, knows everything, can do everything, and has an explanation for everything. His parents are immensely proud of him. It was Betta, Daniele’s daughter, who asked him to return to Naples, to the family home, to look after Mario for a few days while she and her husband Saverio attend a conference. But she could never have imagined what would happen… Between four walls and a balcony, a true duel unfolds, forcing Daniele to confront his own ghosts.

film_appearances.Synopsis: John Jorissen teaches philosophy in a small liberal arts school in the American Midwest, and is writing a book on Spinoza. His life revolves around teaching, writing and spending time with his partner Becca, a fellow professor, and her adolescent son Willie. Jorissen is smart, serious and distant. Something from the past torments him. When his estranged father Melvyn passes away, the sudden appearance of a young man, Miguel Basque, shocks Jorissen at the funeral. It is revealed through flashback that there was an incident between Jorissen and Miguel, the young son of the Jorissen family’s gardener. Melvyn paid Miguel’s father for their silence and private schooling. In return, the family pressed no charges. Wrought with guilt, shame and confusion over his past, as well as the growing suspicion that Spinoza’s God would never pardon his actions, Jorissen purchases Nembutal, a lethal euthanasia powder. Conflicted, Jorissen asks Becca to marry him. Soon after, Becca is approached by Miguel, who feels an obligation to discuss what Jorrisen had done years ago. When she confronts him, Jorissen denies everything. film_appearances.Synopsis: In 1970 two things happened: Russell Crowe stepped onto a film set for the first time and received his first guitar. “Everything starts with music. Everything in my life as a creative person actually begins with music.” In What Love Builds , Crowe gives us a soliloquy set to a lifetime of his own music. Revealing and deeply personal, it shows how music and acting are intrinsic and interconnected through storytelling and performance. What Love Builds is a rare, deep dive into the inspirations behind this legendary and enigmatic artist. Featuring archival footage and photos, What Love Builds traces a journey of street performances, pubs, nightclubs and theatre stages. As his career on screen expands globally, the artist never stops his search for self-expression. “Film is great. It’s a cerebral adventure. You construct the performance in your lounge room, you go and do your job, and then a year to a year and a half later you see the effect of that, the series of emotional points that you may have planned and whether you’ve taken the audience with you or not. Rock and roll is right there and right then. It’s completely immediate and that’s what is exciting about it.” Behind the success, accolades and awards his passion for music and his commitment to the power of storytelling are steadfast – despite the roadblocks, critics and naysayers. His creativity is a perfect confluence – music and acting working in harmony through the peaks and troughs of a career that starts in childhood. Like a sculptor chipping away insecurities to reveal a core form, we watch the man grow and evolve into the master storyteller we know today. This personal fireside chat explodes onto stages from St Kilda to Siena, via Glastonbury Festival and the Whiskey a Go Go. Full of heartfelt candour and self-deprecating humour, What Love Builds connects us to the man as he connects with audiences around the world from Pompeii to Dublin. It’s one of those experiences you didn’t know you needed until you saw it. It leaves an indelible mark.

film_appearances.Synopsis: “Joie de vivre” is an expression that Bernardo Bertolucci was especially fond of. Together, we will explore the legacy of Bertolucci’s cinema: how his films can transform the way people think about cinema, especially those who have yet to discover them – and why certain long-standing interpretations of his work have been profoundly short-sighted and ultimately mistaken. It is a long journey that hops from one place to another around the world, meeting Bertolucci’s longtime producer, Jeremy Thomas, as well as other incredible filmmakers and film experts and lovers who share the same ambition Bernardo had: the courage to see cinema not merely as something regional or national, but as something cosmopolitan and borderless.

film_appearances.Synopsis: Ferrara, the final months of 1943. Pharmacist Barilari – a fascist from the very beginning, struck by paralysis after the March on Rome – looks out of his window at the city, ghostly and shrouded in fog. He observes the fascists attempting to reorganise the party, preparing retaliation and raids. He observes his wife Anna, young, unhappy, and likely searching for another love. But he might, perhaps, pretend not to have seen some of these glimpses of history and city life. Vancini’s debut in narrative cinema won the Award for Best First Feature at the Venice International Film Festival in 1960.
film_appearances.Award Received: Venice Classics Award for Best Restored Film

film_appearances.Synopsis: Minnie is an elegant museum worker who meets long-haired parking lot attendant Moskowitz when he comes to her rescue after a blind date gone bad. This volatile pair forms the centre of an oddball comedy romance, directed by John Cassavetes, about two people who have little in common besides their loneliness. The cast is rounded out with eccentric characters played by Timothy Carey and Val Avery, as well as most of the Cassavetes-Rowland family.

film_appearances.Synopsis: Yonta, a beautiful young woman much admired and the daughter of a former freedom fighter, and her brother Amílcar, named after the leader of the fight for independence – the extraordinary intellectual, agronomist, diplomat, and politician Amílcar Cabral – take part in a new struggle against the burden of the colonial legacy. While Amílcar and the other children embody the unwavering solidarity of African ethics, Yonta is in love with a former freedom fighter and courted by a young man shaped by incompatible European ideals – the blue eyes from a Swedish book that he copies out in an attempt to win her affection.

film_appearances.Synopsis: When Tokiko’s fiancé, Shuichi, announces a desire to become a tuna fisherman, her father Fusajiro, who has been at the trade a long time, becomes enraged, as he thinks the young man is only belittling the occupation. But he persists, and Fusajiro agrees to instruct him in the science. The moment the trawler leaves port Shuichi gets seasick, and Fusajiro laughs. But the young man recovers and they encounter a huge school of tuna. While fishing, Shuichi is seriously injured. He asks for help but Fusajiro, busy fishing, ignores him, thus provoking the young man’s hatred against him...

film_appearances.Synopsis: Depicting the plight of Vietnamese refugees in the form of an action thriller and as the second work in Ann Hui’s Vietnam Trilogy, Woo Yuet dik goo si follows Woo Viet, a Vietnamese veteran who reunites with his long-time pen pal Li Lap-Quan in a refugee camp in Hong Kong. There, he meets and develops a relationship with fellow refugee Shum Ching. The pair attempts to flee to the United States but ends up stranded in Manila’s Chinatown, where local triads force Shum into prostitution and make Woo work as a hired assassin. By setting its two main characters adrift, the film foreshadows the themes of displacement and wandering that preoccupy Hui’s later works. Hui successfully infuses the assassin genre with a serious social message, distinguishing herself as the New Wave director most adept at navigating the balance between commercial viability and artistic expression.
film_appearances.Keywords: vietnamese refugees; hong kong; manila; assassin; prostitution
film_appearances.Selection Status: Officially selected (Venice Classics - Restored Films)

film_appearances.Synopsis: In an apocalyptic Palermo, the Gemelli family is forced to shelter and hide an uncle from Brooklyn. The request comes from the Dwarves mafia clan – and refusing them is simply not an option. The mysterious guest neither speaks, nor sleeps, nor eats, while a cast of strange, unsettling figures circles around him. As in the sketches of Cinico TV, Palermo becomes a desolate landscape inhabited by a brutalised, ghostly humanity. The cultural genocide foretold by Pier Paolo Pasolini has come to pass.

film_appearances.Synopsis: Set in the Roman outskirts in the 1970s, the film portrays the life of a very large family: twenty-five people living in a shantytown. At the centre of the story is the patriarch Giacinto Mazzatella, a one-eyed despot originally from Puglia, who treats his family members with brutality and greed. Family life is marked by conflict, poverty and intrigue. The plot revolves around Mazzatella’s obsession with one million lire (received from the insurance company as compensation for the loss of his eye), which he hides and guards with paranoid jealousy.

film_appearances.Film Title: Valerie and her week of wonders
film_appearances.Synopsis: Set on the threshold between childhood and adulthood, Valerie a týden divů (1970) follows a thirteen-year-old girl whose quiet life with her strict grandmother dissolves into a series of eerie and dreamlike encounters. As Valerie begins to question her own roots, she is drawn into a shifting world where identities blur, time bends, and familiar figures take on disturbing new forms. A mysterious boy named Orlík becomes her guide through this labyrinth of visions, offering both protection and a sense of mystery. The film transforms Vítězslav Nezval’s novel into a visually rich and unsettling fantasy. Blending elements of gothic horror, surrealism, and comingof- age allegory, it reflects the anxieties, desires, and awakening sexuality of its young heroine.
film_appearances.Keywords: girl; grandmother; visions; surreal; sexuality

film_appearances.Synopsis: Born in Leipzig in 1937 to Jewish parents, Anita G., a former telephone operator, fled the GDR for the West in the 1960s. She found a job as a nurse, but after receiving a suspended sentence following a theft, she moved to another city. Working as a sales representative for a record company, she forges order forms, lives beyond her means and becomes her boss’s mistress. However, for the sake of his wife, he breaks off the relationship and reports her to the police. Anita then loses her next job as a chambermaid, tries in vain to take up a university course, and has a shortlived affair with a married senior civil servant. Drifting through West Germany, Anita becomes increasingly unable to find her place in the post-war society.

film_appearances.Synopsis: It is summer in Milan. The city is quiet. Daria and Lia, a mother and her young daughter, go about their daily routine. Daria no longer leaves the house and has created a small ecosystem of plants inside the flat. Lia only goes out to do the shopping and to work on her art project inspired by the myth of Demeter and Persephone. It is the images she films outside her home that lead her, little by little, to recognise her own destiny.

film_appearances.Synopsis: A family of four – Father, Mother, Daughter and Son – arrives at a mysterious house between the ocean and the forest, feeling an unnamed crisis. What begins as a temporary stay stretches into a strange limbo. After an accident leaves Son bedridden, the family turns to a ritual of telling stories about the ocean, stories that seem to make people forget. Haunted by recurring nightmares, Daughter begins to sense that her own missing childhood memories are tied to the house and to a girl in a green dress. As the past surfaces and the boundary between reality and story dissolves, she must choose her way of remembering.
